title: 〜こと (sentence-final instruction) "must / be sure to"
meaning: A rule or instruction in written notices, school rules, and exam directions.
simpleExplanation: Ending a sentence with the dictionary form + こと turns it into a rule or instruction: 教室では日本語で話すこと = "Speak Japanese in the classroom". The negative is ない + こと: 廊下を走らないこと = "Do not run in the corridors". It is a written style, found on notices, school rules, exam papers and to-do lists. It is not used when speaking to someone; in speech you would say 〜てください or 〜なさい.
whenUsed: Classroom and dormitory rules, notices in offices, instructions on exam papers (漢字で書くこと), and memos to yourself. Neutral, impersonal, written. Because it is impersonal, it feels firm but not rude.
formation: V-dictionary + こと: 提出すること (Submit it)
V-ない + こと: 遅れないこと (Do not be late)
Spoken equivalents: 〜てください, 〜なさい, 〜ないでください

examples.ja: 教室では日本語で話すこと。
examples.reading: きょうしつでは にほんごで はなすこと。
examples.note: A classroom rule: dictionary form + こと.

examples.ja: レポートは金曜日までに出すこと。
examples.reading: レポートは きんようびまでに だすこと。
examples.note: A deadline instruction on a notice.

examples.reading: ろうかを はしらないこと。
examples.en: Do not run in the corridors.
examples.note: A prohibition: ない + こと.

examples.ja: （試験の注意）答えはすべて鉛筆で書くこと。
examples.reading: （しけんの ちゅうい）こたえは すべて えんぴつで かくこと。
examples.en: (Exam instructions) Write all answers in pencil.

examples.en: (Dormitory rules) Do not make loud noises after 11 p.m.
examples.note: ない + こと for a rule against something.

similarGrammar.difference: A spoken command from a parent or teacher. こと is the written, impersonal equivalent.
Also sentence-final and written, but ように expresses a hope (合格しますように), not a rule.
こと in the middle of a sentence just makes a noun (話すことが好きだ). Only sentence-final こと is an instruction.

commonMistakes.wrong: （口頭で）明日八時に来ること。
commonMistakes.right: 明日八時に来てください。
commonMistakes.why: こと is for written notices; said aloud to someone it sounds like reading out a rule book.

commonMistakes.wrong: 廊下を走らないでこと。
commonMistakes.why: The negative is the plain ない-form + こと, without で.

commonMistakes.wrong: レポートは金曜日までに出しますこと。
commonMistakes.right: レポートは金曜日までに出すこと。
commonMistakes.why: こと attaches to the dictionary form, never the ます-form.

usageNotes: Notices often list several rules each ending in こと, sometimes numbered.
The exam paper you sit for the JLPT itself uses this style in its instructions.
こと as an instruction has no tense; it is always about what should be done from now.
jlptTips: A sentence in brackets like （学校の規則）or （注意）before the blank tells you the style is a written rule, so a sentence-final こと is the likely answer.
Options may give ことです or ことだ; the bare こと is the notice form. Also check that the verb before こと is in the dictionary or ない-form.
